title: Vulnerability and Security Scanning Tool on AWS Lambda MicroVMs
description: Build an AWS Lambda MicroVM image that runs a vulnerability scanner (Trivy) in a Firecracker-isolated, single-tenant sandbox, one disposable VM per untrusted artifact.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern builds a Lambda MicroVM image containing a vulnerability and security scanner (Trivy). CloudFormation creates the image declaratively with the native AWS::Lambda::MicrovmImage resource, reading a pre-staged code artifact from Amazon S3, and provisions the IAM build and execution roles plus a CloudWatch log group.

Launching a MicroVM from the image is a runtime operation. A caller runs a fresh, single-tenant MicroVM per untrusted artifact (run-microvm), submits the artifact to the scanner over the MicroVM's authenticated HTTPS endpoint (port 8080, JWE token in X-aws-proxy-auth), collects the Trivy JSON report, and terminates the MicroVM.

The scanner reaches vulnerability feeds through the AWS-managed INTERNET_EGRESS connector; ingress is provided per launch via HTTP_INGRESS. Lambda invokes lifecycle hooks on port 9000. Because the pattern provisions only the reusable building blocks, it can be plugged into any trigger: an S3 event, an API, a CI/CD stage, or a queue consumer.
See the GitHub repo README for the run-microvm, auth-token, and /scan commands to launch a MicroVM and scan an artifact.
Terminate any running MicroVMs, then: aws cloudformation delete-stack --stack-name vuln-scanner --region <region>

authors.name: Abhishek Agawane
authors.bio: Abhishek Agawane is a Security Consultant at Amazon Web Services with more than 8 years of industry experience. He helps organizations architect resilient, secure, and efficient cloud environments, guiding them through complex challenges and large-scale infrastructure transformations.
